steps.tx: **Biotin** binds streptavidin and so it distorts immunoassays that use that pair. A sandwich assay such as TSH reads falsely low because the signal falls. A competitive assay such as free T4 reads falsely high. Those two errors together can imitate Graves disease in a person who is actually euthyroid. Patients should stop biotin for at least 48 hours before the blood is drawn.

Patients should stop biotin for at least 48 hours before the blood is drawn.

steps.tx: The **hook effect** is a falsely low result when the analyte is extremely high, classically a giant prolactinoma. Both capture and detection antibodies are saturated, so the sandwich never forms. The true prolactin is unmasked when the sample is diluted in series. **Heterophile antibodies** do the opposite and can falsely raise a sandwich assay by bridging the antibodies without any analyte.

vis.alt: Coronal diagram of a prolactinoma between the cavernous sinuses, under the optic chiasm and pituitary stalk, above the sphenoid sinus.
vis.caption: Sellar anatomy of a prolactinoma. The mass sits under the optic chiasm and between the cavernous sinuses. This drawing does not show the hook effect. Dilution, not the picture, unmasks a falsely low prolactin. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: **Macroprolactin** is a biologically quiet complex of prolactin and immunoglobulin. The assay counts it, but the patient often has little clinical disease. **Polyethylene glycol** precipitation that leaves a recovery below 40 percent means macroprolactin accounts for most of the measured prolactin. Treatment is not required for the high number alone when symptoms and the monomer fraction are quiet.

left.title: True hyperprolactinaemia
points: Look for a prolactinoma or a drug cause

right.title: Macroprolactin
points: Dopamine agonist treatment is not required for the number

steps.tx: The **insulin tolerance test** is the reference stimulation test for cortisol reserve and for growth hormone reserve. It is adequate only if the glucose falls below 40 mg/dL. It is contraindicated in ischaemic heart disease, seizure disorder, and frail older adults. A doctor must be present, and intravenous glucose must be ready before the insulin is given.

steps.tx: A peak growth hormone at or below 5 point 1 mcg/L on an adequate insulin tolerance test supports **adult growth hormone deficiency**, using the Endocrine Society cutoff. The glucagon test is the usual alternative when hypoglycaemia is unsafe. Obesity blunts the growth hormone peak, so a borderline result in an obese adult needs that context and is not read as a simple yes.

left.title: Insulin tolerance test
points: Reference test for adult growth hormone deficiency
Peak at or below 5.1 mcg/L supports deficiency
Unsafe in heart disease or seizures

right.title: Glucagon test
points: Used when insulin hypoglycaemia is unsafe
Does not require a glucose below 40 mg/dL
Obesity can blunt the peak on either test
Still a stimulation test, not a random level

steps.tx: The 1 mg overnight **dexamethasone suppression test** is a screen, not a localisation test. A next-morning cortisol of 1 point 8 mcg/dL, which is 50 nmol/L or higher, is an abnormal result. Do not image the pituitary or the adrenals before the biochemical diagnosis of Cushing syndrome is secure. A random afternoon cortisol is not a screening test.

vis.alt: Four causes of Cushing syndrome: exogenous steroid, pituitary adenoma, ectopic ACTH, and adrenal tumour, beside the clinical features.
vis.caption: Causes of cortisol excess, which the 1 mg dexamethasone test does not separate. Exogenous steroid, a pituitary adenoma, ectopic ACTH, and an adrenal tumour are drawn as different sources. An abnormal screen is a next-morning cortisol of 1.8 mcg/dL (50 nmol/L) or higher. Localisation comes after that screen. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: **Inferior petrosal sinus sampling** separates pituitary Cushing disease from ectopic ACTH secretion. A central to peripheral ACTH ratio of at least 2 before **CRH**, or at least 3 after CRH, supports a pituitary source. It is done only after ACTH-dependent Cushing syndrome is proved. It is not a screening test and it is not used to decide whether Cushing syndrome is present.

steps.tx: **Adrenal vein sampling** is a localisation test for primary aldosteronism after the diagnosis is confirmed and surgery is desired. With cosyntropin, a **selectivity index** of at least 5 shows the catheter is in the adrenal vein. A **lateralization index** of at least 4 supports a unilateral source. Sampling is not required when a young adult has a clear unilateral adenoma and a very high aldosterone.

steps.tx: Choose the test from the picture in front of you. A **stimulation test** is for cortisol deficiency. The left side of the drawing has adrenal atrophy, an ACTH label, and mucosal hyperpigmentation. A **suppression test** is for cortisol excess. The right side has adrenal hyperplasia, a dorsocervical fat pad, and violaceous striae. The drawing has those two pictures. It does not have the stimulation protocol or the overnight suppression cut-off.

steps.tx: A single serum cortisol does not identify the source. The drawing separates four causes of **cortisol excess**: exogenous glucocorticoid with adrenal atrophy, a pituitary ACTH adenoma, ectopic ACTH, and an adrenal tumour with atrophy of the other gland. A suppression test checks whether secretion is autonomous, because autonomous cortisol fails to fall. The drawing has those causes and the body habitus. It does not have the hook effect.
